title.narrative: Lifesaving Rapid Response to Returnees from Sudan to address WASH Needs in Rubkona

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to increase access to life-saving WASH services for anticipated new arrivals of Returnees and Refugees from Sudan crossing from the Panakuach entry point in Rubkona County, South Sudan. This will be achieved by providing safe water, temporary latrines, WASH kits, and desludging of fecal waste at the entry point in Panakuach, in the host community, and at the destination of returnees in Budang Payam in the Rubkona County, which is a destination many of the returnees and refugees are settling in.ltbrgtSince April 2023, 29,635 individuals have been recorded as entering Panakuach, with monthly arrivals reduced in recent months due to flooding. Since flooding has now receded at entry points, the number of returnees and refugees is anticipated to increase again. Therefore, in readiness to launch an immediate response at the entry points when the situation escalates while at the same time responding to priority needs in the host communities, Concern will prepare itself for a 48-hour response by completing the procurement process and pre-selection of potential suppliers. The response will be activated when the number of arrivals increases to 80-100 at Panakuach, and Concern will submit a release request to the South Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SSHF). Concern will collaborate with the WASH Cluster, IOM Camp Management, RRC, and local administration in Payangai to avoid duplication of efforts and ensure a coordinated response.ltbrgtAs part of the response, Concern will construct gender-segregated temporary sanitation facilities and ensure water through mobile trucking that will be stored in plastic tanks with a capacity of 1,000-2,000 liters at the transit center. Concern will also provide soap, buckets, and MHM/ Dignity Kits to newly arrived returnees and refugees. Concern will support the new arrivals at the destination through temporary latrines, WASH kits, and water supply, including repair of the existing borehole and increasing the network of the existing water supply system. Concern will target 10,000 individuals, including returnees/refugees and the host communities. Host communities have been included in the project to mitigate the risks of inter-communal violence between host communities and returnees over access to assistance.ltbrgtConcern will display feedback, complaints, and response numbers at the distribution points and the WASH facilities to promote community participation and identify specific needs. Concern's staff will use community feedback to adapt the activities within the project's scope. During water supply, persons with special needs (PWDs, Pregnant and breastfeeding women, and the elderly) will be prioritized. During the latrine construction at the transit center and in the household, Concern will add disability-friendly infrastructural features (i.e., ramps, supporting handles, railing, etc.).ltbrgtlt/pgt
